title: SLO Convergence: cross-stack error budget reconciliation and automated throttle gates
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Create an Initiative-level tracker and automated gate system that reconciles error budgets across affected stacks (hosted API, Dedicated pools, Private deployments) and surfaces coordinated throttles/rollbacks when aggregate risk across teams exceeds defined thresholds. This ticket scopes the PM work: definition of reconciliation rules, stakeholder workflow, observable signals, and acceptance criteria.

Background:
We have multiple SLO owners measuring SLIs at different scopes: per-service, per-model, per-region, and per-customer tier. When a platform-level degradation occurs (e.g., KV cache storms, kernel hotpath regressions, autoscaler misconfiguration), individual error budgets may not independently breach thresholds but aggregate risk across stacks requires coordinated mitigation. Current playbooks are manual and rely on pager-driven decisions. This initiative reduces toil and speeds coordinated responses.

Goals: 
- Define deterministic reconciliation rules for combining error budgets across scopes (weighted by traffic, customer tier, and dependency graph).
- Design automated gate actions (rate-limit throttles, canary rollback triggers, model downgrade routes) with safe defaults and manual override paths.
- Build an initiative tracker UI in Console to show live aggregated error budget runway and recommended mitigation actions.
- Integrate with incident runbooks, oncall dashboards, and rollout policies so teams can execute with fewer escalations.

Scope (what PM owns):
- Requirements and decision log for weighting algorithm and thresholds.
- UX/acceptance criteria for Console tracker and alert templates.
- Stakeholder alignment across Runtime, Serving, Dedicated, and Observability teams.
- Pilot plan with two production workloads (hosted text-generation and embeddings) and one Dedicated customer group.

Out of scope for this ticket (handled in separate ENG work items):
- Implementation of kernel-level mitigations and autoscaler code.
- RBAC changes for Console (unless a gating UX is required).

Acceptance criteria: 
- A documented reconciliation algorithm (Confluence) with examples and edge cases.
- Prototype Console tracker mockups validated with oncall and SRE (3 interviews).
- Playbook describing automated gate actions, with at least one automated throttle implemented in staging.
- End-to-end test that simulates simultaneous SLI degradations and verifies recommended actions.

Risks & trade-offs: 
- Overly aggressive automatic gates could increase user-facing errors; introduce conservative thresholds and require manual approval for high-impact customers.
- Aggregation logic may hide localized degradations; trackers must allow drill-down to per-service SLIs.

Cross-team dependencies: 
- Observability (ENG-88421) for metric rollup and aggregation endpoints.
- Runtime (ENG-90233) for hook points to enact throttles and rollbacks.
- Console UX (DES-56100) for tracker surfaces and interaction design.

Deliverables: 
- Decision doc: Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/SLO+Convergence+Decision+Log
- Prototype mockups in Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/Redwood/SLO-Convergence-Tracker
- Staging throttle implementation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/6248
- Playbook & runbook: https://runbooks.redwood.ai/slo-convergence/playbook

Notes: 
- Estimate reflects PM work to stitch stakeholders and create acceptance criteria; implementation will spawn ENG tickets after design sign-off.
- Pilot target: deploy to us-west hosts and Dedicated pool DP-9 for pilot customers.
